author: Zhang and Zhu
name_in_asr: 阿奢理贰伽蓝 (Xiyu ji); 阿奢理儿寺 (the Life)
asr_identification: Kizilgaha caves (克孜尔尕哈石窟, the place of worship) with the Bozkhana temple site (博其罕那佛寺, the living quarters), c. 10 km NW of the Pilang old city (皮朗古城), Kucha county, Xinjiang
evidence: Position and distance, from the 3rd national survey of immovable cultural relics and the authors' fieldwork; no excavation. Shahetur (夏合吐尔, the Duldur-Aqur ruin on the Weigan/Muzat river) lies 30 km SW of Pilang, against the Xiyu ji's 'NW of the assembly place, across a river' and the Life's 'NW of the city'; Kizilgaha lies c. 10 km NW. The king fed Xuanzang before noon and then went with him to the monastery, and on departure 'the whole city' saw him off, so the monastery was within half a day of the capital. 淹停 in the Life means only 'stayed' (no flood); the river crossed is the Kucha river between Pilang and Kizilgaha, so Pelliot's argument from the river for Shahetur fails. A saṃghārāma combines cult place and living quarters, so the residence is the Bozkhana surface temple (Ran Wanli et al. 2011 survey report).
quote: 第一，夏合吐尔遗址在皮朗古城西南 30 千米，与“会场西北，渡河至阿奢理贰伽蓝”及“食讫过城西北阿奢理儿寺”相矛盾，而克孜尔尕哈石窟在皮朗西北约 10 千米处，更接近文献记载。…因此，“阿奢理贰伽蓝”的礼拜场所当在克孜尔尕哈石窟，而生活区则在博其罕那。
note: Differs from the study and Mizutani (Duldur-Aqur, medium, on position alone; Ji and Pelliot the same). The bearing argument is real: Duldur-Aqur is W to SW of Kucha, Kizilgaha NW. Not decisive either way: nothing names the monastery at either site, and Pelliot's Tocharian B library at Duldur-Aqur is not discussed. Other views listed (not argued): Kutluk-Ordar (库特鲁克·欧尔达), Bozkhana alone (博特罕那). Leaves 01.06.04 open between the two.

author: Zhang and Zhu
name_in_asr: 阿奢理贰; 克孜尔尕哈石窟 as 龟兹'王寺'
asr_identification: Kizilgaha caves, Kucha county, as above
evidence: Royal patronage at Kizilgaha, after the cave catalogue (2009) and Jia Yingyi: caves 13 and 14 show an earth deity holding up a Kucha king and queen, unique among the Kucha caves; cave 11 has royal donor figures; the great-image niche of cave 23 faces Pilang; a Tocharian (Kuchean) inscription in cave 25 reads 'in the 19th regnal year of king Suvarṇadeva (苏伐叠), year of the tiger, 6th month, 8th day, came to this holy place to worship'. Suvarṇadeva reigned 624-646, Xuanzang passed in 628; the authors link this to the Life's royal uncle 智月 (Mokṣagupta's monastery). No inscription names the monastery.
quote: 第四，克孜尔尕哈石窟是龟兹“王寺”，与“阿奢理贰”地位相称。…第 25 窟侧壁发现龟兹文题记：“国王苏伐叠在位第十九年，虎年六月八日，来此圣地谒佛祈愿。”
note: Adds evidence of royal worship at Kizilgaha under the king of Xuanzang's time, which suits the Xiyu ji's royal foundation (王以為奇特也，遂建伽藍); but a king's visit is not the monastery's name, and the Life's 智月 is not tied to the site. Not site evidence in the study's sense; the place stays open (see :1).

author: Zhang and Zhu
asr_identification: Pilang old city (皮朗古城), Kucha county, Xinjiang
evidence: States that the 'great city' of the Xiyu ji is the Pilang old city, citing the Xinjiang Institute's brief report on the 2016 excavation of the Kucha old city (龟兹故城, Xinjiang wenwu 2017(2)); no evidence given in the article itself.
quote: 《大唐西域记》所述“阿奢理贰”寺在龟兹都城西北，二者隔河相望。“大城”为龟兹都城，即今皮朗古城
note: Agrees with Ji (capital probably the Pilang old city) and the study (Kucha, district). Points to a 2016 excavation of the city (not read here); the study's district-level medium is unchanged.

author: Zhang and Zhu
name_in_asr: 跋禄迦 (姑墨); 盐关道
asr_identification: Road from Kucha to Bālukā: the Yanshui gully (盐水沟) road by Baicheng to Aksu, roughly provincial road 307 (Kucha-Baicheng); not the Zhejue pass road (柘厥关道) of the Xin Tang shu
evidence: Distances: the Xin Tang shu (Jia Dan) gives Anxi (Kucha) to Gumo by the Zhejue pass as 420 li; the Xiyu ji and the Life give 600+ li; the 180 li difference shows a different road, the long main road vs the short cut. Qing sources: in the Khoja revolt the Kucha hakim beg named two routes west, the ford of the Weigan (short cut) and the Qizil gobi main road through the northern pass; Khoja Jahan fled by the latter; Woren in 1851 went from Kucha by the Yanshui gully and Qizil to Baicheng. Pelliot's 1907 Kuchean wooden tablets from the Yanshui gully beacon give the name 盐关. The capital of Bālukā is not named.
quote: 玄奘西行跋禄迦之道路即“盐关道”，可通拜城、阿克苏一带，与今 307 省道基本一致。…《新唐书·地理志》中“安西”至“姑墨”为“四百二十里”，《大唐西域记》《三藏法师传》记载均为“六百余里”，二者相差一百八十余里，显然并非同一路线
note: Adds a route argument the study does not have. It does not choose a capital for 01.07 (open among Aksu/Wensu, Kara-yulgun, Baicheng etc.); a longer northern road by Baicheng would suit the 600 li without moving the capital. The study's identification (Aksu region, capital undecided) is unchanged.

author: Hassan, Shah and Yatoo
asr_identification: Zehanpore stupa site, Baramulla district, Jammu and Kashmir (after Ray 1969)
evidence: None of its own: repeats, after S. C. Ray (1969), that Xuanzang lodged at the Jushka (Huṣkara) Vihara at Ushkur and then visited the Jayendra Vihara, 'historically linked' to the Zehanpore stupa.
quote: During his travels, Hiuen Tsang lodged at the Jushka Vihara (Ushkur) before visiting the Jayendra Vihara, a site historically linked to the archaeological stupa at Zehanpore (Ray, 1969).
note: new = 闍耶因陀羅寺 (Jayendra monastery), a Life-only place, not in places.tsv. The Life puts it in the capital (至都，止闍耶因陀羅寺, T50 2053), i.e. Srinagar (03.06.01a), not near Baramula, so the link to Zehanpore does not fit Xuanzang's account. 護瑟迦羅寺 at Ushkur (the first night after the stone gate) is also Life-only.

author: Hassan, Shah and Yatoo
asr_identification: Zehanpore village (34°10'42.87"N 74°15'19.98"E), Baramulla district, c. 10 km from Baramulla town, right (north) bank of the Jhelum, Jammu and Kashmir
evidence: A Buddhist complex with three stupas in a line (Stupa 1-3; site plan) on the right bank of the Jhelum, c. 10 km from Baramulla, on the old route to Gandhara and Central Asia; the main stupa is threatened by bank erosion (measured from Landsat 1976-2022 and Google Earth; worst 1989-2000, from instream mining). No date, excavation or inscription given; the paper does not connect the site with the Xiyu ji's Mahāsāṃghika monastery.
quote: The study was carried out at Zehanpore village (34°10'42.87"N and 74°15'19.98"E) in Baramulla district, Kashmir, about 10 km from the Baramulla town on the right bank of the Jhelum (Figure 2)…The site plan shows the linear arrangement of Stupa 1, Stupa 2, and Stupa 3.
note: Bears on 03.06.11 only by position (the bearing is the coder's, not the paper's): the Xiyu ji puts the monastery 140-150 li W of the capital, N of the great river and S of the mountains; Zehanpore is on the N bank inside Mizutani's Baramula-Rampur stretch, where he reported 'no monastery site on the N bank'. Srinagar to Zehanpore is c. 51 km in a straight line, long for 145 li at 0.25-0.3 km/li. A candidate, untested; agrees with the study's area, no site identified (low).

author: Azad
asr_identification: Kumrahar and Bulandibagh, Patna, Bihar (as Pāṭaliputra)
evidence: Catalogue of seals and sealings from the Patna excavations (Spooner 1912-13: 20 seals, 9 of them matrices, at Kumrahar above the Mauryan pillared hall; Altekar and Mishra 1959: 1 seal and 50 sealings; Sinha's four Patna sites: none). Monastic pieces at Kumrahar: a Mauryan clay matrix 'Dīghavata palama saghasa'; a Kushan sealing with a building plan and 'Saghasa'; Gupta sealings 'Śrī-ārogyavihāre bhikṣusaṁghasya' (with potsherds 'ārogyavihāre' and '[Dha]nvantareḥ' from the same trench) and 'Śrī suapi bṛhadvihāra bhikṣusaṁghasya' with the Sarnath deer-and-wheel device. No legend names Pāṭaliputra.
quote: Besides it, some seals and potsherds allude to the fact that the area was also a monastic settlement…So, together with the matrix of seals, sealings, building architecture, etc. makes it clear that it was monastic-cum-commercial centre right from Ashoka's regime to the Gupta period.
note: Agrees with the study (Patna/Kumrahar, high) and Mizutani; no location argument. Adds inscribed evidence of Buddhist monasteries at Kumrahar into the Gupta period, consistent with Xuanzang's ruined city with hundreds of old monastery, temple and stupa sites (伽藍、天祠及窣堵波，餘址數百). Does not bear on the unlocated sub-sites (08.02.03, 08.02.05, 08.02.x1-x6).

author: Azad
evidence: Gupta sealing of a 'sanatorium monastery' at Kumrahar, taken as one of the monasteries giving medical care that Faxian describes.
quote: It probably would be the one among those monasteries where medical treatments used to provide, which Fa Hien described.
note: Faxian's hospital at Pāṭaliputra is not in the Xiyu ji; no bearing on a Xiyu ji place.
